annotations.title: Check a JSON Schema, and whether OpenAI, Claude and Gemini strict modes accept it

description: Use when the user asks whether a JSON Schema is valid, or whether it will work with OpenAI Structured Outputs or function calling with strict: true, Claude structured outputs or strict tool use, or Gemini structured output (response_json_schema), or is writing a tool or function schema, an MCP inputSchema, a response_format, or a schema exported from Zod or Pydantic (signals: "Invalid schema for response_format", "strict mode error", "Claude returns 400 for my schema", "will this schema work with OpenAI", "Gemini ignores maxLength", "additionalProperties false", "all fields must be required"). First checks the schema against its draft: type names like "int", "required": true on a property, misspelt keywords, unresolvable $ref, invalid regex, impossible ranges. Then checks each provider's documented rules: OpenAI (every property in required, additionalProperties false on every object, root an object and not anyOf, no allOf/not/if, at most 5000 properties, 10 levels, 1000 enum values, documented formats only), Claude (additionalProperties false, no minimum/maximum/multipleOf/minLength/maxLength, minItems only 0 or 1, no recursion, at most 24 optional and 16 union-typed parameters per request, regex without lookarounds or backreferences), Gemini (minLength, maxLength, uniqueItems, minProperties and similar are dropped without an error). Returns per provider a verdict (ok, warnings, fails), each issue with its JSON Pointer path, rule, fix and the provider's doc URL, plus a converted copy the provider accepts (optional fields made required and nullable for OpenAI, unsupported constraints moved into descriptions the way the official SDK helpers do), and counts (properties, depth, optional and union-typed parameters). Example: {"schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string","maxLength":40},"days":{"type":"integer","minimum":1}},"required":["city"]},"providers":["openai","anthropic"]}. Rules are from each provider's docs, checked 2026-11-18; providers can change them, and very large schemas can still hit unpublished size limits.

draft.description: Force a draft: 2020-12, 2019-09, 7, 6 or 4. Default: from $schema, else 2020-12.

include_converted.description: Include a converted copy for each provider that does not accept the schema as is. Default true.

providers.description: Which providers to check. Default: all three.

schema.description: The JSON Schema to check, as a JSON object (not a string).
